repos.title: InternVL: Scaling up Vision Foundation Models and Aligning for Generic Visual-Linguistic Tasks
repos.paper_summary:
**This document outlines the LaTeX guidelines for author responses in arXiv submissions, emphasizing structure, formatting, and clarity.**
- Addresses *rebuttal* limits: one-page PDFs allowed to address reviewers' comments without adding new contributions.
- Enforces a *two-column layout*: dimensions of 6.875 inches wide by 8.875 inches high for text areas, ensuring readability.
- Highlights *equation numbering importance*: necessary for clear reference, avoiding overlaps with main paper.
- Provides guidance on *figure inclusion*: centers graphics, advises on font sizing and line widths for clarity in printed copies.
- Maintains *anonymity rules*: prohibiting personal identifiers and external links in the response to ensure blind review integrity.

repos.title: MindSearch: Mimicking Human Minds Elicits Deep AI Searcher
repos.paper_summary:
MindSearch is an LLM-based multi-agent framework for web information seeking and integration. It comprises a WebPlanner and multiple WebSearchers. The WebPlanner models problem-solving as the iterative construction of a directed acyclic graph, where nodes represent atomic sub-questions and edges denote dependencies. The planner generates Python code to add nodes and edges, dispatching independent sub-questions to parallel WebSearchers. Each WebSearcher performs hierarchical retrieval: it rewrites queries, executes searches via APIs like Bing, selects relevant pages from search results, and summarizes content for the planner.

Evaluated on closed-set QA (Bamboogle, Musique, HotpotQA) using GPT-4o and InternLM2.5-7B, MindSearch outperforms baselines including raw LLMs and ReAct-style search. For GPT-4o, the average accuracy across datasets is 59.8%, compared to 53.5% without search and 55.1% with ReAct. For InternLM2.5-7B, the average is 49.2%, compared to 28.9% and 42.9%. In open-set QA evaluations by human experts, MindSearch responses were preferred over ChatGPT-Web and Perplexity.ai Pro in depth and breadth, though not factuality. Limitations include potential hallucinations due to long-context processing and reliance on specific search API access.

repos.title: GaussianAvatar: Towards Realistic Human Avatar Modeling from a Single Video via Animatable 3D Gaussians
repos.paper_summary:
GaussianAvatar reconstructs animatable human avatars from a single monocular video using 3D Gaussian Splatting. The method represents the human body as a set of canonical 3D Gaussians that are reposed to arbitrary poses via forward skinning, bypassing the inverse skinning ambiguity inherent in NeRF-based approaches. A dynamic appearance network, combined with an optimizable feature tensor, predicts pose-dependent properties such as surface offsets and colors to capture cloth wrinkles. Because the rendering is differentiable with respect to motion parameters, the system jointly optimizes SMPL pose estimates and avatar appearance during training, correcting inaccuracies in initial monocular motion tracking.

On the People-Snapshot dataset, the full model achieves a PSNR of 30.98 dB, outperforming InstantAvatar (29.53 dB) and HumanNeRF (26.90 dB). On the more challenging DynVideo dataset, it reaches 28.58 dB PSNR compared to 20.31 dB for InstantAvatar. Rendering speed is 35 FPS, significantly faster than the 3.87 FPS of InstantAvatar. The authors note that inaccurate foreground segmentation can cause boundary artifacts, and the method struggles to model loose garments like dresses due to reliance on standard SMPL skinning weights.

repos.title: Data-Juicer: A One-Stop Data Processing System for Large Language Models
repos.paper_summary:
Data-Juicer is a data processing system for Large Language Models (LLMs) that provides over 50 composable operators to construct, clean, and evaluate data recipes for pre-training and fine-tuning. The system decouples specific data types and auxiliary models into standardized modules—Formatters, Mappers, Filters, and Deduplicators—allowing users to freely compose pipelines via configuration files or code. It integrates with distributed computing frameworks like Ray and Beam, employing optimizations such as operator fusion, caching, and checkpointing to handle massive datasets efficiently.

Empirical evaluation shows that LLMs trained on Data-Juicer-refined pre-training data achieve an average score improvement of up to $7.45\%$ across 16 benchmarks compared to baselines. In some cases, models trained on only $43\%$ of the original data quantity outperform those trained on full datasets. For fine-tuning, models using Data-Juicer-processed data exhibit a $10.3\%$ higher win rate in pairwise GPT-4 evaluations against leading competitors, while utilizing $56.8\%$ fewer data samples. System-level tests report up to $88.7\%$ reduction in single-machine processing time, $77.1\%$ memory savings, and $7.91\times$ acceleration in distributed processing. Limitations include reliance on external model-based filtering tools and the computational cost of evaluating large-scale data recipe impacts.

repos.title: Reproducible scaling laws for contrastive language-image learning
repos.paper_summary:
This paper establishes reproducible power-law scaling relationships for contrastive language-image pre-training (CLIP) using the public LAION dataset and open-source OpenCLIP code. The authors trained models ranging from ViT-B/32 to ViT-g/14 on up to 2.3 billion image-text pairs, varying model size, data scale, and samples seen. They evaluate performance on zero-shot classification, retrieval, linear probing, and fine-tuning.

The study finds that downstream accuracy follows a power law with respect to total compute. For zero-shot ImageNet classification, the scaling coefficient is $-0.11$ for LAION-trained models versus $-0.16$ for OpenAI’s WIT-400M-trained models. Conversely, for MS-COCO retrieval, LAION models show stronger scaling ($-0.08$) than OpenAI models ($-0.05$). This indicates that training distribution significantly influences task-specific scaling behavior. Using these laws, the authors predict that a ViT-G/14 model trained on 68 billion samples would achieve 81.9% zero-shot top-1 accuracy on ImageNet. Limitations include low sampling density in the scale space due to compute constraints and the inability to fully tune hyperparameters at larger scales.

repos.title: Grounding DINO: Marrying DINO with Grounded Pre-Training for Open-Set Object Detection
repos.paper_summary:
Grounding DINO is an open-set object detector that extends the DINO Transformer-based architecture with language inputs to detect arbitrary objects specified by category names or referring expressions. The model integrates a feature enhancer, language-guided query selection, and a cross-modality decoder to fuse vision and text modalities at three distinct stages: the neck, query initialization, and head. It employs a sub-sentence level text representation using attention masks to prevent interaction between unrelated category names during training.

Pre-trained on large-scale datasets including COCO, OpenImages, GoldG, and caption data, Grounding DINO achieves 52.5 AP on the COCO zero-shot detection benchmark without using any COCO training images. It sets a new record on the ODinW zero-shot benchmark with a mean 26.1 AP. On RefCOCO/+/g, it reaches 90.56% accuracy after fine-tuning. Limitations include inferior performance on rare LVIS categories compared to DetCLIPv2 and the generation of false positives in some cases.

repos.title: Sentence-BERT: Sentence Embeddings using Siamese BERT-Networks
repos.paper_summary: Sentence-BERT (SBERT) modifies BERT to generate fixed-size sentence embeddings suitable for cosine similarity, reducing the time to find the most similar pair in a collection of 10,000 sentences from approximately 65 hours to about 5 seconds. The method adds a pooling operation to the BERT output and fine-tunes the network using siamese or triplet structures on Natural Language Inference data. On seven Semantic Textual Similarity tasks, SBERT achieves an average Spearman rank correlation of 74.89, outperforming InferSent by 11.7 points and Universal Sentence Encoder by 5.5 points. For supervised STS benchmark evaluation, SBERT reaches 84.67 Spearman correlation, comparable to the BERT cross-encoder baseline of 84.30. On SentEval transfer learning tasks, SBERT improves the average accuracy by 2.1 points over InferSent. A limitation is that SBERT underperforms the BERT cross-encoder on the Argument Facet Similarity dataset in cross-topic settings, where it drops by about 7 points because it cannot directly compare unseen argumentative contexts.

repos.title: TokenEconomizer: Experience-Driven Black-Box Cost Control for Coding Agents
repos.paper_summary: TokenEconomizer is an external controller that reduces token costs for black-box coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot CLI) over sequences of tasks within the same repository, without modifying model weights or agent code. It applies three meta-strategies whose policies are learned from completed traces: activating repository-specific micro-skills, pruning loaded tools that are never called, and intervening in failure loops using a turn budget set from successful prior runs, with an LLM judge deciding whether to redirect or stop. Evaluation covers 277 SWE-Bench tasks across six repositories in five agent–model settings, plus 102 Web-Bench tasks and 200 security-auditing tasks. On SWE-Bench, mean cache-aware cost falls by 18.4–30.9% including controller overhead, and Pass@1 rises in four of five settings; the one drop is 1.0 percentage point on Opus 4.8. Reduced reasoning effort lowers Pass@1 by 1.8–10.3 points in comparison. On Web-Bench and the security benchmarks, cost falls by 16.0–21.2% and 6.4–19.6%, with Pass@2 and detection F1 comparable to default. Limitations: the controller can make incorrect decisions (stale skills, wrongly pruned tools, mistaken loop detection), and SWE-Bench task streams are independent fixes rather than real user sessions.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Recurring coding-agent costs in shared repositories motivate an external controller that learns from completed tasks.

digest_headlines.heading: Cost Profiling and Analysis of Fixed Cost-control Strategies
digest_headlines.headline: Fixed cost-control strategies give mixed results by repository, and traces reveal three sources of removable cost.

digest_headlines.heading: TokenEconomizer
digest_headlines.headline: TokenEconomizer selects micro-skills, tool masks, and turn budgets per repository using confirmation, retirement, and failure-loop rules learned from traces.

digest_headlines.heading: Experiments
digest_headlines.headline: On the software-engineering benchmark, TokenEconomizer cuts mean cost 18.4–30.9% across five settings, raising Pass@1 in four.

digest_headlines.heading: Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: Existing agent cost methods are typically fixed and task-local, whereas TokenEconomizer adapts cost control from completed traces.

digest_headlines.heading: Limitations and Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: Stale skills, wrongly pruned tools, and mistaken loop detections remain possible, and streams are not real user sessions.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: The appendix covers extended discussion, cost-profiling protocol, controller configuration, task selection, examples, and harness customization.

repos.title: TokenPilot: Cache-Efficient Context Management for LLM Agents
repos.paper_summary:
TokenPilot is a context management framework for LLM agents that reduces inference costs by aligning text compression with prompt cache continuity. It operates at two granularities: Ingestion-Aware Compaction stabilizes the prompt prefix by replacing volatile runtime variables with static placeholders and stripping structural noise from tool responses before they enter the context window; Lifecycle-Aware Eviction monitors context segments in batches, offloading them only when their estimated residual utility expires. This prevents the layout mutations that typically invalidate hardware KV caches.

Evaluated on PinchBench (123 tasks) and Claw-Eval (161 tasks) using GPT-5.4-mini, TokenPilot reduces total inference cost by 61% and 56% in isolated mode, and 61% and 87% in continuous mode, respectively, while maintaining competitive task accuracy. For instance, on Claw-Eval continuous mode, it lowers cost from USD 81.52 to USD 10.58. The system requires backend support for prefix caching and relies on a model-based estimator that may misclassify segments under ambiguous interaction patterns. Additionally, performance gains depend on grouping same-category tasks into contiguous sessions, as heterogeneous streams exhibit lower prefix reuse rates due to frequent tool schema changes.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Text pruning cuts tokens but mutates prompt layouts and breaks cache reuse, so TokenPilot pairs ingestion stabilization with lifecycle eviction.

digest_headlines.heading: Background
digest_headlines.headline: Serving cost is modeled as discounted cache-hit tokens plus full-cost miss tokens across isolated and continuous task modes.

digest_headlines.heading: TokenPilot
digest_headlines.headline: The framework stabilizes prompt prefixes at ingestion and evicts context segments only after their residual utility expires, in batches of turns.

digest_headlines.heading: Experiments
digest_headlines.headline: On Claw-Eval isolated mode, TokenPilot scores 63.1 at USD 2.27 cost, versus Vanilla's 64.5 at USD 5.16.

digest_headlines.heading: Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: Prior work covers static text compression, passive memory retrieval and summarization, and runtime paging and scheduling of context.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: The conclusion states that TokenPilot cuts inference cost in both modes without sacrificing task effectiveness.

digest_headlines.heading: Limitations
digest_headlines.headline: Limits include estimator misclassification, tuning of threshold tau and batch size, dependence on prefix caching, and weaker reuse on shuffled streams.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: The appendix lists benchmark statistics, cost formula and prices, baseline settings, hyperparameters, estimator prompts, and mixed-category results.

repos.title: Reinforcement Learning for Versatile, Dynamic, and Robust Bipedal Locomotion Control
repos.paper_summary: This paper presents a dual-history reinforcement learning controller for bipedal robots, enabling diverse locomotion skills including walking, running, and jumping on the Cassie robot. The method uses a long-term input/output history encoder to adapt to dynamics changes and contact events, combined with a short-term history fed directly to the policy network to handle high-frequency control needs. Training follows a three-stage curriculum: single-task learning, task randomization, and dynamics randomization. In simulation ablations, the dual-history architecture outperforms baselines like RMA and state-feedback-only policies under randomized dynamics parameters. Real-world experiments demonstrate zero-shot sim-to-real transfer, with the robot maintaining stable standing for 459 days, completing a 400-meter dash, and executing jumps up to 1.4 meters forward and 0.44 meters high. The authors identify task randomization as a key source of robustness distinct from dynamics randomization, promoting compliant recovery behaviors. Limitations include difficulty achieving precise velocity tracking during fast running and the requirement for specific reference motions; for instance, backward jumps could not be learned from a forward-jumping reference alone.
